title: cost-opt: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token unit cost across common workloads by providing better out-of-the-box batching/caching defaults, adding quantization profile presets for popular model families, and shipping unit-economics (UEcon) tooling that surfaces the cost impact of config choices. This PR bundles three coordinated changes: 1) Autotune and default configuration changes for the request router and runtime batching layer: new default max_batch_ms reduced from 20->12 for latency-sensitive routes, adaptive minibatch sizing by model family, and a prefix-KV caching TTL and warmup policy to enable higher cache hit rates for common prompt prefixes. 2) Quantization profile presets: adds q8_256 and q4_0_mixed presets for transformer-decoder families with validated perf/regression profiles. Profiles include kernel hints for GPU selection and fallbacks for CPU-only nodes. 3) Unit-econ tooling: a new /console/cost-sim endpoint and CLI tool (redwood-uecon) to estimate per-request cost given throughput, batch latency SLO, cache hit rate, and quant profile. It also integrates into the Console cost/latency breakdown and adds a small guided UX for recommended defaults. Checklist: - [x] Define new defaults and document rationale - [x] Add runtime flags and server-side validation - [x] Add quant profiles + unit tests - [x] Add UEcon CLI and Console integration - [x] Performance validation (latency and tokens/sec) - [x] E2E tests in perf-canary NOTE: This is a non-breaking change for config semantics; existing deployments keep explicit user configs unless they opt into "autotune_defaults": true.
commits: feat(runtime): add autotune defaults for batching and cache warmup
perf(runtime): adaptive minibatch sizing by model family
feat(models): add quant profiles q8_256 and q4_0_mixed with validation test vectors
feat(uecon): add redwood-uecon CLI and /console/cost-sim endpoint
docs: document defaults, quant profiles, and Console UX
test(perf): add canary test scenario for mixed chat/generation workload
chore: bump telemetry schema for cache hit metrics

ci_checks: CI summary: unit tests (pass), lint (pass), integration (flaky -> retried -> pass), perf-canary (pass), e2e (pass). One integration test failed on first run due to timing race; rerun passed. All checks green before merge.
performance_summary: Mixed chat/generation scenario: median p50 latency change for sampled routes: -8ms (improved). 95th percentile latency: within SLO. Tokens/sec: +12% on average with q8_256, +18% with q4_0_mixed at comparable quality in internal eval. Cache hit rate increased from 22%->46% after warmup heuristics in synthetic traces.
rollback_plan: If a regression is detected post-merge we will: 1) Toggle 'autotune_defaults' feature gate off globally (control plane route) 2) Revert quant profiles via model registry rollback (tagged artifacts) 3) Roll back Console UX via feature flag. Ops playbook updated with metrics to watch (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cache_hit_rate, per-route cost).
release_notes: Added autotune defaults for batching and KV prefix caching to improve out-of-the-box throughput and reduce per-token cost; introduced validated quantization profile presets for common models (q8_256, q4_0_mixed); shipped unit-economics simulation tooling (redwood-uecon) and Console integration to help teams estimate cost tradeoffs.
